mathematical_result.name: QFORM-MINORITY-AXIS-NONCENTRAL-RIGIDITY-v1
mathematical_result.statement_short: For Q=G1^2+G2^2-cG3^2 with equal Gaussian variance and a mean shift only along the minority-sign coordinate, the global density never exceeds the centered cone-tip 1/(2s sqrt(1+c)); a fixed nonzero shift has an explicit strict loss. A cap-one three-bank finite family with spectrum {1,1,-(1+1/m)} converges uniformly in output density to this limit.
mathematical_result.key_mechanism: use the exponential law of two centered equal-variance Gaussian squares, complete the square in the minority coordinate, reduce the negative two-sheet branch to an erfc expression, and control it by erfc(x)<=e^{-x^2}; transfer to source-valid cap-one bank sums through a uniform unimodal quadratic-phase L1 Fourier envelope.

partner_result_applied.actual_application: At theta=1/100 the partner sequence has liminf norm >=3sqrt(2)e^{-3/100}=4.117251705266084..., while the same-spectrum axial-drift bank family has limsup <=3sqrt(2)e^{-(3-2sqrt(2))/4}=4.064507827950592.... The exponent order is certified by 1296>1250.

unresolved_implication: This excludes only minority-axis noncentrality in an equal-positive-eigenvalue diffuse limit. Off-axis means coupled to anisotropy, several non-collinear macroscopic shared rows, surviving non-Gaussian components, and extra active spectrum remain possible witness mechanisms.
next_step: Attack off-axis noncentrality/anisotropic negative two-sheet peaks or a two-macroscopic-row surviving non-Gaussian limit; do not repeat centered fragmentation or axial-shift controls.
